hints.title: Set the logical target
hints.body: Necessary but not sufficient means every parallelogram has the condition, while some non-parallelogram also has it.
hints.recap: You need one valid direction and one failed converse.
hints.pitfall: A familiar sufficient test may be too strong for the requested answer.
hints.pause: Which properties hold in every parallelogram?

recall.reminder: Necessity tests <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mtext>target</mtext><mo>⇒</mo><mtext>condition</mtext></mrow></math>; insufficiency needs condition without target.

hints.title: Keep track of which side pair
hints.body: Compare the side conditions carefully: equality and parallelism may concern the same opposite-side pair, or two different opposite-side pairs. Keep those relations attached to the correct sides when sketching.
hints.recap: Those two statements have different strength.
hints.pitfall: Do not silently replace two different side pairs with the same pair.
hints.pause: For each side condition that survives your necessity check, try to construct a quadrilateral satisfying it and determine whether it must be a parallelogram.

recall.reminder: Preserve the objects attached to each relation when reading a compound statement.

hints.title: Check both logical directions
hints.body: Use a parallelogram that is neither a rectangle nor a rhombus to test necessity. For any surviving condition, look for a non-parallelogram satisfying it.
hints.recap: Necessary means every parallelogram has the property; sufficient means the property forces a parallelogram.
hints.pitfall: Special parallelograms can hide which properties are necessary.
hints.pause: Identify the condition passing exactly the required pair of tests.

recall.reminder: Necessary means every parallelogram has the property; sufficient means the property forces a parallelogram.

solution:
Every parallelogram has PQ=SR and PS parallel to QR, so A is necessary. It is not sufficient: an isosceles trapezium can have these properties without being a parallelogram.

For example, P=(0,0), Q=(1,−1), R=(1,2), S=(0,1) gives PQ=SR=2 and PS parallel to QR, but PS and QR have lengths 1 and 3.

B is both necessary and sufficient because the same opposite side pair is equal and parallel. C is not necessary: a parallelogram need not have all sides equal. D is not necessary: its diagonals need not be equal.

A is necessary but not sufficient.
knowledgePattern: Distinguish opposite-side conditions belonging to the same or different pairs
